summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with right-sided abdominal and flank pain described as a burning sensation, initially of unknown cause. Imaging ruled out acute abdominal pathology, diverticulitis, or obstruction. A vesicular rash developed along the right T5/6 dermatome, leading to a diagnosis of localized varicella zoster (shingles) by dermatology, despite a negative viral swab. She was treated with IV acyclovir, later transitioned to oral valacyclovir, with clinical improvement. Liver enzymes were elevated, attributed to possible hepatic zoster or GVHD, prompting an increase in prednisone from 15mg to 20mg daily and initiation of Bactrim for PCP prophylaxis. Epigastric pain emerged late in the admission, managed with Maalox and ranitidine after normal amylase, lipase, and imaging. The patient stabilized, pain improved with pregabalin, and she was discharged home on updated medications with follow-up planned.
problems: Herpes zoster without mention of complication
Peripheral stem cells replaced by transplant
Nonspecific elevation of levels of transaminase or lactic acid dehydrogenase [LDH]
